# W17 · How to end chat sessions so we don't leak resources on the sever

## Summary

Chats no longer hold server processes for ever. Closing a chat, or an agent exiting by itself, now ends the agent's whole process group, the screen's exit waits until every chat's group is gone, a page-run turn that times out is killed with everything it started, and a background chat nobody has used for 30 minutes (or `DFS_CHAT_IDLE_SECONDS`) is closed by the screen. An "End chat" button on the page closes the agent and keeps the conversation, and both it and "New chat" refuse while an answer is in progress. The Goal is met; a real claude resuming after an idle close was not run, and the page and button were not seen rendered because no browser starts here.

## Goal

How to end chat sessions so we don't leak resources on the sever

## Tree

### W17.1 · Closing a chat kills everything it started
Status: confirmed
Approach: **The question**: when a background chat ends, does anything the agent started survive it?
- **Why it matters**: `Relay.close` in `scripts/ptyrelay.py` sends SIGHUP and then SIGKILL to the agent's pid only. The agent's own children (its shell, tool servers) stay running after the chat is closed. That is a leak on the server.
- **What this node does**: the agent is the leader of its own process group (`pty.fork` makes it a session leader). `close` signals the whole group (`os.killpg`), SIGHUP first and SIGKILL after two seconds.
- **How we will know it worked**: a new test in `scripts/test_ptyrelay.py` runs an agent that starts a background `sleep`, closes the relay, and checks the `sleep` is gone. It must fail on the old code first.
Determination: Confirmed: `Relay.close` now signals the agent's whole process group, and the new test (a child that ignores the hang-up) failed before the change and passes now; a child that does not ignore it was already ended by the kernel when the agent died, so the leak is only for children that ignore SIGHUP.

### W17.2 · A web chat turn that times out is killed with its children
Parent: W17.1
Status: confirmed
Approach: **The question**: when a page-run turn (`Chats.turn` in `scripts/chat.py`) hits `TURN_TIMEOUT`, does the claude it started die?
- **Why it matters**: `subprocess.run(..., timeout=)` kills only `run.sh`'s pid. `run.sh` ends by `exec`ing claude, but claude's own children can still survive.
- **What this node does**: run the turn with `Popen(start_new_session=True)` and on timeout `killpg` the group, then collect its output.
- **How we will know it worked**: a test in `scripts/test_chat.py` uses a stub that leaves a child behind and hangs. After a short timeout the child must be gone.
Determination: Confirmed: a page-run turn now runs in its own process group (`run_group` in `chat.py`) and the group is killed on timeout; the new test failed before the change and passes, and the only failing test in `test_chat.py` (`elsewhere`) fails without the change too.

### W17.3 · Idle background chats are closed
Parent: W17.2
Status: confirmed
Approach: **The question**: how long may a background chat sit unused before the server closes it?
- **Why it matters**: today a chat the page opened lives until the screen exits or someone presses "New chat". Every chat opened and forgotten keeps one claude process for good.
- **What this node does**: `Relay` records its last use (output or a send). `ChatHost.reap(idle)` closes chats unused for longer than the limit, never one that is attached or answering. The screen's poll in `scripts/tui.py` calls it. Closing keeps the session id, so the next message resumes the same conversation from its transcript.
- **How we will know it worked**: tests in `test_ptyrelay.py` for reap (idle closed, active and attached kept) and one in `test_chat.py` that a message after a reap resumes the session.
Hypothesis: A background chat unused for 30 minutes can be closed with nothing lost, because the next message starts the agent again on the same session and the talk resumes from its transcript. Wrong if a resumed session loses something the author relied on, or if 30 minutes closes chats people still use. .dfs/artefacts/62c3c730-f004-43eb-a4bc-e5b95366b79c.html
Evidence:
- for: `ChatHost.ensure` already starts a fresh agent for a scope whose relay ended, and `chat.claim` resumes the saved session id when its transcript exists; `Chats.send` goes through that path, so a message after a close reaches a resumed agent. `test_ptyrelay` (reap closes only the idle one, then `ensure` starts a new agent) passes.
- against: no test starts a real claude on a resumed session after a reap; the resume path was read, not run. Whether 30 minutes is the right limit is a choice, not something a check settles.
Determination: Confirmed: `ChatHost.reap` closes chats unused for `IDLE_LIMIT` (30 minutes; never one that is attached or just used), the screen's poll calls it, and the `test_ptyrelay` tests pass; the page was checked structurally only since no browser starts here.

### W17.4 · The page can end a chat without losing it
Parent: W17.3
Status: confirmed
Approach: **The question**: how does a person end a chat today without throwing the conversation away?
- **Why it matters**: only "New chat" ends the agent, and it also deletes the session record. There is no way to free the process and keep the talk.
- **What this node does**: a `chat/end` action (`chat.py`, `web.py`, a button in `scripts/web/index.html`) closes the running agent and keeps the session id.
- **How we will know it worked**: `test_web.py`/`test_chat.py` check the agent is closed, the messages stay, and a later send resumes. The last node says whether the Goal is met.
Determination: Confirmed, and the Goal is met: `Chats.end` and `POST /api/chat/end` close the running agent and keep the session, an "End chat" button on the chat sheet calls it, and `test_chat` and `test_web` pass (the one failing `test_chat` test, `elsewhere`, fails without the change too); the button was not seen rendered since no browser or node starts here.

### W17.5 · Fix: agents' process groups outlive the screen and an agent that exits by itself
Parent: W17.1
Status: confirmed
Approach: The group kill lives only in `Relay.close` (`scripts/ptyrelay.py`), which returns at once when `not self.live`, and its SIGKILL runs in a daemon thread after `time.sleep(2)`. Read: (a) `ChatHost.close_all` is defined but nothing calls it (grep `close_all` in `scripts/`: only the definition and tests), so when the screen (`tui.py`) exits, the chats' agents are left to the kernel's hang-up on the pty master closing, which an agent's child that ignores SIGHUP (the very case W17.1's test covers) survives; (b) if an agent exits on its own (`_pump` sees EOF, sets `fd = None`), nothing signals the group, so children it left behind (nohup'd tool servers) keep running, and `ChatHost.ensure` just replaces the dead relay; (c) at screen exit the 2 s daemon thread would not get to send the SIGKILL even if `close_all` were called. Fix: when the screen quits, close every chat and kill the groups synchronously (SIGKILL after a short bounded wait in the calling thread, not a daemon), and make `_pump` end (killpg SIGKILL/HUP) whatever is left in the group once the agent has been reaped, guarding against the pid being reused (only while the group still exists, e.g. check `os.killpg(pid, 0)` right after the waitpid). Add tests in `scripts/test_ptyrelay.py`: an agent that leaves a HUP-ignoring child and exits by itself leaves no child; `close_all` leaves none without waiting on a daemon thread. Check the screen's quit path in `tui.py` calls it.
Determination: Confirmed: an agent's group is now killed as soon as the agent is seen to have exited (before it is reaped, so the id cannot be reused), `ChatHost.close_all` hangs up on all chats together and returns only when their groups are gone, and both new `test_ptyrelay` tests failed before the change and pass now; the screen already called `close_all` on exit (the Approach's first reading, that nothing called it, was wrong), but its kill ran in a daemon thread and never got to run.

### W17.6 · Fix: End chat kills a background chat that is in the middle of an answer
Parent: W17.4
Status: confirmed
Approach: `Chats.end` in `scripts/chat.py` refuses only when `scope in self.busy` (a page-run turn). A chat running on the screen is answering when `w.chat_active(scope)` is true; `Chats.state` counts that as `busy` (`talking`), and the page shows it as answering, but `end` goes straight to `w.chat_close(scope)` and kills the agent mid-answer, so the answer the person was waiting for is lost, while the error text ("it is still answering: wait for it") says the guard is meant to stop exactly that. The test in `test_chat.py` uses a stub whose `chat_active` is always False, so it cannot catch this. Fix: refuse in `end` (and, since it has the same hole and the same message, in `clear`) when the walker's `chat_active(scope)` is true, return the same ValueError, and add a test with a stub screen where `chat_active` is True that expects the ValueError and that `chat_close` was not called. Also make the page's `chatend` handler show that error (it already toasts `e.message`).
Determination: Confirmed: `Chats.end` and `Chats.clear` now refuse (the same "still answering" error) while the screen's agent is answering, the new test failed before the change and passes, and the page's `chatend` handler already toasts that error; the one other failing `test_chat` test fails without the change too.

### W17.7 · Minor findings from the review
Parent: W17.5
Status: confirmed
Approach: Fix these beside W17.5 and W17.6:
- `Relay.close` now sends SIGKILL to the group unconditionally after 2 s, where it was guarded by `self.fd is not None`; the group id may by then belong to an unrelated process (covered by the pid-reuse check in W17.5, keep it when reworking).
- `reap_chats` in `tui.py` has no test (the reap itself does); a stub-UI test that `poll` calls it and logs the event would cover it.
- The "End chat" toast says the next message picks the conversation up even when no agent was running; it could say nothing in that case.
- `IDLE_LIMIT` (30 minutes) cannot be set without editing the code; an env override would do.
- The "End chat" button and the toast were never rendered (no browser here); look at the sheet once a browser is available.
Determination: Confirmed: the group kill after two seconds is now skipped once the agent is reaped (done in the earlier fix), `reap_chats` and the poll call have tests, `End chat` returns `ended` and the page toasts only when an agent was running, and `DFS_CHAT_IDLE_SECONDS` sets the idle limit; the sheet was still not seen rendered since no browser starts here, and the 10 `test_screen` errors and the one `test_chat` failure are there without the change too.

### W17.8 · Fix: the screen's chats are not closed when the screen is stopped by SIGTERM or SIGHUP
Parent: W17.5
Status: open
Approach: `main` in `scripts/tui.py` (about line 4930) calls `ui.chat_host.close_all()` only in the `finally` after `ui.loop()`. Nothing in `tui.py`, `walk.py` or `web.py` installs a SIGTERM or SIGHUP handler (grep `signal.signal` finds none), so a screen that is stopped by `kill`, a service manager, or a dropped ssh/terminal (SIGHUP) dies at once with no `finally`. The agents then get only the kernel's hang-up when the pty master closes, and a child that ignores SIGHUP survives. That is the exact leak W17.1 and W17.5 set out to close, on the most usual way a server process is stopped. Fix: in `main`, install handlers for SIGTERM and SIGHUP (before `ui.loop()`, restored after) that raise `SystemExit` or `KeyboardInterrupt` in the main thread so the existing `finally` runs `close_all`. Check that curses still restores the terminal. Add a test: start a process that builds a `ChatHost` with an agent that leaves a HUP-ignoring child, deliver SIGTERM to it, and check the child is gone. It must fail on the current code first.

### W17.9 · Minor findings from the review
Parent: W17.8
Status: open
Approach: Fix these beside W17.8:
- `Relay.idle_for` counts only output and sends as use: if a real claude repaints a spinner or status line while idle, the 30-minute reap never fires. Look when a real claude is available.
- `Relay.hangup` checks `live` and then calls `killpg` without a lock; a pump that reaps the agent between the two leaves a tiny pid-reuse window. The 2 s kill is guarded, the hang-up is not.
- `ChatHost.relays` keeps a dead `Relay` per scope until `ensure` replaces it, and `reap` looks only at live ones; small and bounded by the number of scopes, but `reap` could drop dead entries.
- The "End chat" button and toast were never rendered (no browser here); look at the sheet once one is available.
- `test_chat.py` `test_it_will_not_send_while_the_screens_chat_is_open_on_the_session` (`elsewhere`) fails; the sessions say it fails without the change too, which was not re-run here, so check it.

# W17 · How to end chat sessions so we don't leak resources on the sever

## Summary

Ending a chat now leaves nothing behind. Closing a background chat hangs up on the agent, its process group and everything it started (even helpers that left the group), kills what is left after two seconds, and lets go of the server's end of the terminal once the agent is gone; when the screen exits it waits for those kills, so chats that ignore the hang-up do not outlive it. Chats that quit on their own are forgotten by the host, and a page turn is killed with what it started when it times out, ends, or the server stops. Left out: a chat the author leaves open runs until the screen ends or "New chat" is pressed, since no idle timeout was asked for, and helpers already re-parented to init, or left by a chat that quit by itself, cannot be found; both limits are stated as an assumption for the author. One existing test in `test_chat.py` fails with and without these changes.

## Goal

How to end chat sessions so we don't leak resources on the sever

## Tree

### W17.1 · Closing a chat ends everything it started and frees our side
Status: confirmed
Approach: **The question**
- When `Relay.close()` (scripts/ptyrelay.py) ends a chat, what is left running or held open?

**Why it matters**
- A probe showed a leak: if a process the agent started has left the agent's process group (`setsid`, as a tool runner or helper may), it keeps the pty open. The agent stays a zombie, the master fd stays open and the `_pump` thread stays blocked in `read` until that helper exits. `close()` only signals the agent's pid.

**What this node does**
- `close()` collects the agent's live descendants (walking `/proc` parent links) before signalling, sends SIGHUP to the process group and then SIGKILL to the group and to each collected descendant after a short grace.
- The reaper also closes our master fd and reaps the agent itself, so our fd, thread and zombie are freed even if something escaped.
- Limit: a process already re-parented to init before `close()` is not reachable this way; the node says so in its Determination.

**How we will know it worked**
- New tests in `scripts/test_ptyrelay.py` start an agent whose helper runs under `setsid`; red before the change (fd stays open, agent zombie, helper alive), green after (fd freed, agent reaped, helper gone).
Determination: Confirmed: `close()` now hangs up on the agent, its group and its descendants, kills what is left after two seconds, and `_pump` lets go of our pty end and reaps the agent once it is gone; both new tests failed before and pass now, and what had already been re-parented to init before `close()` is still out of reach.

### W17.2 · The chat host forgets chats that ended by themselves
Parent: W17.1
Status: confirmed
Approach: **The question**
- What keeps an ended chat's `Relay` object in `ChatHost.relays` (scripts/ptyrelay.py)?

**What this node does**
- A chat that exits on its own (the author quits the agent, or it crashes) stays in `relays` until the same scope is asked for again. `get`, `live_scopes` and `close_all` drop entries that are no longer live, after making sure each is closed.

**How we will know it worked**
- A test in `scripts/test_ptyrelay.py`: an agent that quits leaves no entry in `host.relays` after `get`/`live_scopes`.
Determination: Confirmed: `ChatHost` now drops ended chats on `get`, `ensure` and `live_scopes`; the new test failed before and passes now, with all 12 ptyrelay tests passing.

### W17.3 · Page turns and chats end with the server
Parent: W17.2
Status: confirmed
Approach: **The question**
- When the web page's server stops (`Handle.stop`, `web.main` after Ctrl-C), what happens to a turn in flight (`Chats.turn` runs `run.sh --chat-turn` via `subprocess.run`)? And to chats started from the page?

**Why it matters**
- The turn runs in a daemon thread, so exiting the server abandons the `claude -p` process it started; it runs on, unseen, until it finishes. The web-only server also never closes background chats.

**What this node does**
- `Chats` runs each turn in its own session (`start_new_session=True`), remembers the process, kills its group on timeout, and gets a `close_all()` that kills in-flight turns; `Handle.stop` calls it (and the walker's chat close) so a stopped server leaves nothing behind.

**How we will know it worked**
- Tests in `scripts/test_chat.py` with the stub agent: a turn in flight at `close_all()` has its process gone; a timed-out turn leaves no process.
Determination: Confirmed, and the Goal is met: `Chats.run_turn` runs each page turn in its own session, a timeout and `Chats.close_all()` (called by `Handle.stop`) kill the whole group, and the two new tests failed before and pass now; `Chats.clear` still refuses while a turn runs, as its existing test requires.

### W17.4 · Fix: closing chats as the screen exits does not wait for the kill, so HUP-ignoring chats survive
Parent: W17.1
Status: confirmed
Approach: `Relay.close()` (scripts/ptyrelay.py) sends SIGHUP at once but does the SIGKILL of the group and descendants from a daemon thread (`reap`) after up to GRACE seconds. `tui.main` calls `ui.chat_host.close_all()` in its `finally` and the process then exits, so the daemon thread dies before the SIGKILL ever happens. Checked: a `ChatHost` chat running `bash -c "trap '' HUP; sleep 301 & wait"`, `close_all()` then the interpreter exiting: both the bash and the `sleep` were still running 3s later. Fix: let `ChatHost.close_all` (and so the screen exit) wait for the kills to finish, e.g. have `close()` expose the reaper thread and join it (bounded by GRACE plus a margin), or kill synchronously after the grace in `close_all`; keep the single-chat `close()` (New chat) non-blocking. Add a test in scripts/test_ptyrelay.py that runs `close_all()` on a chat whose agent and helper ignore SIGHUP and asserts both are gone when it returns (red before).
Determination: Confirmed: `ChatHost.close_all` now hangs up on every chat and waits for each one's kill (bounded by the grace plus a margin), while `ChatHost.close` and `Relay.close` stay non-blocking; the new test with a HUP-ignoring agent and helper failed before and passes now, with all 13 ptyrelay tests passing.

### W17.5 · Hypothesis: closing is only on an explicit end, and only reaches what is still below the agent
Parent: W17.1
Status: confirmed
Approach: W17.1 (and the Summary) narrow the Goal "how to end chat sessions so we don't leak resources" without a Hypothesis: (a) a chat the author leaves open is never closed by idle time (no timeout was asked for); (b) processes already re-parented to init before `close()` are out of reach, and when an agent quits by itself (W17.2) its helpers are not hunted either. This could be wrong if the author expects idle chats to be reaped, or expects leftover helpers of a chat that ended by itself to be killed. State both as a Hypothesis on W17.1 with its page, what would show it wrong (a leaked process or pty found after a chat the author left idle or that quit on its own), and the evidence to date.
Hypothesis: A chat is closed only on an explicit end (New chat, the screen exiting), never by idle time; and closing reaches only what is still below the agent, so helpers of a chat that quit by itself, or re-parented to init earlier, are left alone. Wrong if you expect idle chats to be reaped or the helpers of a chat that quit on its own to be killed, or a leaked process or pty is found after such a chat. .dfs/artefacts/1c94e0fd-208b-49fd-a17d-4b36e97c4423.html
Evidence:
- for: a `Relay` running `sleep 303` was still live after 4s, and `scripts/ptyrelay.py` has no timer that ends a chat: nothing reaps an idle one.
- for: an agent that exited on its own (rc 0) left its `setsid` helper running (state S) 2s later: nothing hunts it.
Determination: Confirmed as the state of the work: the two limits are real, now stated as a Hypothesis with its page for the author to accept or overturn.

### W17.6 · Minor findings from the review
Parent: W17.4
Status: confirmed
Approach: One line per finding:
- `Chats.run_turn` registers the process in `procs` only after `Popen`, so a `close_all()` in that gap misses a just-started turn.
- A turn that finishes normally leaves any helper still in its group alive; `kill_group` runs only on timeout or `close_all`.
- `Relay.close`'s reaper calls `killpg(pid, SIGKILL)` unconditionally after the grace, even if the agent was reaped long before, so a reused pid could be hit (very unlikely).
- W17.3's Approach says `Handle.stop` also does "the walker's chat close"; it only calls `Chats.close_all()` (the TUI closes its own `chat_host`), so that sentence is stale.
- `test_chat` has one failing test (`test_it_will_not_send_while_the_screens_chat_is_open_on_the_session`); it fails here too, and its failing before the change rests on the session's word.
Determination: Confirmed: `Chats.run_turn` now starts and registers its process under the lock and kills the group when a turn ends, and the pty reaper no longer signals a reaped agent's pid; the helper-left-behind test failed before and passes now, the `test_chat` failure also fails on the base commit, and the stale W17.3 sentence is left since a determined node does not change.

### W17.7 · Hypothesis: a page turn that ends takes everything it started with it
Parent: W17.6
Status: open
Approach: W17.6 changed `Chats.run_turn` (scripts/chat.py) so that `kill_group(p)` runs when a turn finishes normally, not only on timeout or `close_all`: any process the `claude -p` turn left running (a dev server or watcher the author asked the agent to start from the page, say) is SIGKILLed the moment the turn returns. The Goal ("don't leak resources") does not say that such a process is a leak rather than the thing the author asked for, and W17.6 is a "Minor findings" node with no Hypothesis. It also differs from the screen's chat, where a chat that quits by itself leaves its helpers alone (W17.5). State it as a Hypothesis with its page: a page turn's leftovers are leaks, not work the author wants kept; wrong if the author expects a process started from the page chat to outlive its turn, or the two kinds of chat to treat leftovers alike. Evidence to date: test_chat.test_a_turn_that_ends_takes_what_it_left_running_with_it (stub leaves a `sleep 300` that is gone after the turn).

### W17.8 · Minor findings from the review
Parent: W17.6
Status: open
Approach: One line per finding:
- `Handle.stop` (scripts/web.py) calls `Chats.close_all()` and only then `server.shutdown()`, and `close_all` sets no flag: a page `send` that arrives after it (the server still serves for up to ~0.5s, handler threads are daemons) starts a turn in its own session that nothing kills when the process exits. Fix: a `closed` flag on `Chats` that `send`/`turn` refuse after `close_all`, checked under the lock in `run_turn` before `Popen`; add a test that `send` after `close_all` starts no process.
- `Chats.close_all` also misses a turn thread started by `send` but not yet at `Popen` (same flag closes it).
- `_pump` (scripts/ptyrelay.py) only reaps a gone agent when the pty is idle for 0.5s, so a helper that keeps writing holds the pump thread and our pty end until it stops (close() still kills it after the grace, so only an un-closed, self-quit chat is affected).
- `kill_group` signals `killpg(p.pid)` after the turn's process was reaped; if its group is empty the pid could in principle be reused by an unrelated group leader (very unlikely).
- No test covers the `Chats.close_all` "dropped" path where the turn thread returns without calling `on_change`.
- W17.3's Approach still says `Handle.stop` does "the walker's chat close"; it only calls `Chats.close_all()` (determined nodes are history, so say it in the final summary instead).
- `test_chat.test_it_will_not_send_while_the_screens_chat_is_open_on_the_session` fails in this environment (`running_elsewhere` finds no `claude` process: "coreutils: unknown program 'claude ...'"); note it in the Summary as it is, since it is not from this task.

# W17 · How to end chat sessions so we don't leak resources on the sever

## Goal

How to end chat sessions so we don't leak resources on the sever

## Tree

### W17.1 · Closing a chat kills everything it started
Status: confirmed
Approach: **The question**: when a background chat ends, does anything the agent started survive it?
- **Why it matters**: `Relay.close` in `scripts/ptyrelay.py` sends SIGHUP and then SIGKILL to the agent's pid only. The agent's own children (its shell, tool servers) stay running after the chat is closed. That is a leak on the server.
- **What this node does**: the agent is the leader of its own process group (`pty.fork` makes it a session leader). `close` signals the whole group (`os.killpg`), SIGHUP first and SIGKILL after two seconds.
- **How we will know it worked**: a new test in `scripts/test_ptyrelay.py` runs an agent that starts a background `sleep`, closes the relay, and checks the `sleep` is gone. It must fail on the old code first.

### W17.2 · A web chat turn that times out is killed with its children
Parent: W17.1
Status: confirmed
Approach: **The question**: when a page-run turn (`Chats.turn` in `scripts/chat.py`) hits `TURN_TIMEOUT`, does the claude it started die?
- **Why it matters**: `subprocess.run(..., timeout=)` kills only `run.sh`'s pid. `run.sh` ends by `exec`ing claude, but claude's own children can still survive.
- **What this node does**: run the turn with `Popen(start_new_session=True)` and on timeout `killpg` the group, then collect its output.
- **How we will know it worked**: a test in `scripts/test_chat.py` uses a stub that leaves a child behind and hangs. After a short timeout the child must be gone.

### W17.3 · Idle background chats are closed
Parent: W17.2
Status: confirmed
Approach: **The question**: how long may a background chat sit unused before the server closes it?
- **Why it matters**: today a chat the page opened lives until the screen exits or someone presses "New chat". Every chat opened and forgotten keeps one claude process for good.
- **What this node does**: `Relay` records its last use (output or a send). `ChatHost.reap(idle)` closes chats unused for longer than the limit, never one that is attached or answering. The screen's poll in `scripts/tui.py` calls it. Closing keeps the session id, so the next message resumes the same conversation from its transcript.
- **How we will know it worked**: tests in `test_ptyrelay.py` for reap (idle closed, active and attached kept) and one in `test_chat.py` that a message after a reap resumes the session.
Hypothesis: A background chat unused for 30 minutes can be closed with nothing lost, because the next message starts the agent again on the same session and the talk resumes from its transcript. Wrong if a resumed session loses something the author relied on, or if 30 minutes closes chats people still use. .dfs/artefacts/62c3c730-f004-43eb-a4bc-e5b95366b79c.html
Evidence:
- for: `ChatHost.ensure` already starts a fresh agent for a scope whose relay ended, and `chat.claim` resumes the saved session id when its transcript exists; `Chats.send` goes through that path, so a message after a close reaches a resumed agent. `test_ptyrelay` (reap closes only the idle one, then `ensure` starts a new agent) passes.
- against: no test starts a real claude on a resumed session after a reap; the resume path was read, not run. Whether 30 minutes is the right limit is a choice, not something a check settles.

### W17.4 · The page can end a chat without losing it
Parent: W17.3
Status: confirmed
Approach: **The question**: how does a person end a chat today without throwing the conversation away?
- **Why it matters**: only "New chat" ends the agent, and it also deletes the session record. There is no way to free the process and keep the talk.
- **What this node does**: a `chat/end` action (`chat.py`, `web.py`, a button in `scripts/web/index.html`) closes the running agent and keeps the session id.
- **How we will know it worked**: `test_web.py`/`test_chat.py` check the agent is closed, the messages stay, and a later send resumes. The last node says whether the Goal is met.

### W17.5 · Fix: agents' process groups outlive the screen and an agent that exits by itself
Parent: W17.1
Status: confirmed
Approach: The group kill lives only in `Relay.close` (`scripts/ptyrelay.py`), which returns at once when `not self.live`, and its SIGKILL runs in a daemon thread after `time.sleep(2)`. Read: (a) `ChatHost.close_all` is defined but nothing calls it (grep `close_all` in `scripts/`: only the definition and tests), so when the screen (`tui.py`) exits, the chats' agents are left to the kernel's hang-up on the pty master closing, which an agent's child that ignores SIGHUP (the very case W17.1's test covers) survives; (b) if an agent exits on its own (`_pump` sees EOF, sets `fd = None`), nothing signals the group, so children it left behind (nohup'd tool servers) keep running, and `ChatHost.ensure` just replaces the dead relay; (c) at screen exit the 2 s daemon thread would not get to send the SIGKILL even if `close_all` were called. Fix: when the screen quits, close every chat and kill the groups synchronously (SIGKILL after a short bounded wait in the calling thread, not a daemon), and make `_pump` end (killpg SIGKILL/HUP) whatever is left in the group once the agent has been reaped, guarding against the pid being reused (only while the group still exists, e.g. check `os.killpg(pid, 0)` right after the waitpid). Add tests in `scripts/test_ptyrelay.py`: an agent that leaves a HUP-ignoring child and exits by itself leaves no child; `close_all` leaves none without waiting on a daemon thread. Check the screen's quit path in `tui.py` calls it.

### W17.6 · Fix: End chat kills a background chat that is in the middle of an answer
Parent: W17.4
Status: confirmed
Approach: `Chats.end` in `scripts/chat.py` refuses only when `scope in self.busy` (a page-run turn). A chat running on the screen is answering when `w.chat_active(scope)` is true; `Chats.state` counts that as `busy` (`talking`), and the page shows it as answering, but `end` goes straight to `w.chat_close(scope)` and kills the agent mid-answer, so the answer the person was waiting for is lost, while the error text ("it is still answering: wait for it") says the guard is meant to stop exactly that. The test in `test_chat.py` uses a stub whose `chat_active` is always False, so it cannot catch this. Fix: refuse in `end` (and, since it has the same hole and the same message, in `clear`) when the walker's `chat_active(scope)` is true, return the same ValueError, and add a test with a stub screen where `chat_active` is True that expects the ValueError and that `chat_close` was not called. Also make the page's `chatend` handler show that error (it already toasts `e.message`).

### W17.8 · Fix: the screen's chats and their process groups outlive a screen that is killed by a signal
Parent: W17.5
Status: open
Approach: W17.5 made `ChatHost.close_all` (SIGHUP then SIGKILL of each agent's group, synchronously) run from the `finally` at the end of `main()` in `scripts/tui.py` (~line 4937). That `finally` runs only on a normal quit or a Python exception. A screen on a server is mostly ended by a signal: SIGHUP when the ssh session or terminal drops, SIGTERM from `kill`, a service stop. `grep -n "signal\.\|SIGTERM\|SIGHUP\|atexit" scripts/tui.py` finds no handler, and Python's default for both is to terminate the process without running `finally`, so `close_all` never runs. The agents get only the kernel's hang-up when their pty master closes, which reaches the session leader and its foreground group, and not the group's children that ignore it: the exact case W17.1 and W17.5 set out to fix, so those children leak on the commonest way a screen ends. Fix: in `main()` (before `curses.wrapper`, or inside `main`), handle SIGTERM and SIGHUP by raising `SystemExit` (or `KeyboardInterrupt`) so the existing `finally` runs, and keep `close_all` bounded (it waits at most about 2 + 2 s). Add a test in `scripts/test_screen.py` or `test_ptyrelay.py`: a child python process that builds a `ChatHost`, starts an agent leaving a HUP-ignoring `sleep`, installs the same handler, is sent SIGTERM and SIGHUP in turn, and afterwards the `sleep` must be gone. Confirm the test fails without the handler.

### W17.9 · Fix: a timed-out page turn can wait for ever on a child that left its group
Parent: W17.2
Status: open
Approach: `run_group` in `scripts/chat.py` kills the turn's process group on timeout and then calls `p.communicate()` with no timeout. A descendant that left the group (it called `setsid`, as a daemonised tool server does) is not killed and still holds the stdout/stderr pipes, so `communicate()` does not return until that process ends. I ran `chat.run_group(["sh","-c","setsid sleep 6 & sleep 60"], "", None, None, 1)`: it raised `TimeoutExpired` only after 6 s, the life of the escaped child. With a long-lived one the turn thread never returns, `Chats.turn`'s `finally` never clears `scope` from `self.busy`, and the chat is stuck "answering" for ever (End chat and New chat both refuse), the page's poll thread held. Fix: after the kill, collect with a bound (`p.communicate(timeout=…)`, a few seconds), and on a second timeout close the pipes (`p.stdout.close()`, `p.stderr.close()`) and `p.wait()` so the call always returns; keep the original exception. Add a test in `scripts/test_chat.py` with a stub whose escaped child outlives the call (`setsid sleep 30 &` then hang) and assert `run_group` returns within a few seconds of the timeout and the chat is no longer busy.

# W17 · How to end chat sessions so we don't leak resources on the sever

## Goal

How to end chat sessions so we don't leak resources on the sever

## Tree

### W17.1 · Closing a chat ends everything it started and frees our side
Status: confirmed
Approach: **The question**
- When `Relay.close()` (scripts/ptyrelay.py) ends a chat, what is left running or held open?

**Why it matters**
- A probe showed a leak: if a process the agent started has left the agent's process group (`setsid`, as a tool runner or helper may), it keeps the pty open. The agent stays a zombie, the master fd stays open and the `_pump` thread stays blocked in `read` until that helper exits. `close()` only signals the agent's pid.

**What this node does**
- `close()` collects the agent's live descendants (walking `/proc` parent links) before signalling, sends SIGHUP to the process group and then SIGKILL to the group and to each collected descendant after a short grace.
- The reaper also closes our master fd and reaps the agent itself, so our fd, thread and zombie are freed even if something escaped.
- Limit: a process already re-parented to init before `close()` is not reachable this way; the node says so in its Determination.

**How we will know it worked**
- New tests in `scripts/test_ptyrelay.py` start an agent whose helper runs under `setsid`; red before the change (fd stays open, agent zombie, helper alive), green after (fd freed, agent reaped, helper gone).

### W17.2 · The chat host forgets chats that ended by themselves
Parent: W17.1
Status: confirmed
Approach: **The question**
- What keeps an ended chat's `Relay` object in `ChatHost.relays` (scripts/ptyrelay.py)?

**What this node does**
- A chat that exits on its own (the author quits the agent, or it crashes) stays in `relays` until the same scope is asked for again. `get`, `live_scopes` and `close_all` drop entries that are no longer live, after making sure each is closed.

**How we will know it worked**
- A test in `scripts/test_ptyrelay.py`: an agent that quits leaves no entry in `host.relays` after `get`/`live_scopes`.

### W17.3 · Page turns and chats end with the server
Parent: W17.2
Status: confirmed
Approach: **The question**
- When the web page's server stops (`Handle.stop`, `web.main` after Ctrl-C), what happens to a turn in flight (`Chats.turn` runs `run.sh --chat-turn` via `subprocess.run`)? And to chats started from the page?

**Why it matters**
- The turn runs in a daemon thread, so exiting the server abandons the `claude -p` process it started; it runs on, unseen, until it finishes. The web-only server also never closes background chats.

**What this node does**
- `Chats` runs each turn in its own session (`start_new_session=True`), remembers the process, kills its group on timeout, and gets a `close_all()` that kills in-flight turns; `Handle.stop` calls it (and the walker's chat close) so a stopped server leaves nothing behind.

**How we will know it worked**
- Tests in `scripts/test_chat.py` with the stub agent: a turn in flight at `close_all()` has its process gone; a timed-out turn leaves no process.

### W17.4 · Fix: closing chats as the screen exits does not wait for the kill, so HUP-ignoring chats survive
Parent: W17.1
Status: confirmed
Approach: `Relay.close()` (scripts/ptyrelay.py) sends SIGHUP at once but does the SIGKILL of the group and descendants from a daemon thread (`reap`) after up to GRACE seconds. `tui.main` calls `ui.chat_host.close_all()` in its `finally` and the process then exits, so the daemon thread dies before the SIGKILL ever happens. Checked: a `ChatHost` chat running `bash -c "trap '' HUP; sleep 301 & wait"`, `close_all()` then the interpreter exiting: both the bash and the `sleep` were still running 3s later. Fix: let `ChatHost.close_all` (and so the screen exit) wait for the kills to finish, e.g. have `close()` expose the reaper thread and join it (bounded by GRACE plus a margin), or kill synchronously after the grace in `close_all`; keep the single-chat `close()` (New chat) non-blocking. Add a test in scripts/test_ptyrelay.py that runs `close_all()` on a chat whose agent and helper ignore SIGHUP and asserts both are gone when it returns (red before).

### W17.5 · Hypothesis: closing is only on an explicit end, and only reaches what is still below the agent
Parent: W17.1
Status: confirmed
Approach: W17.1 (and the Summary) narrow the Goal "how to end chat sessions so we don't leak resources" without a Hypothesis: (a) a chat the author leaves open is never closed by idle time (no timeout was asked for); (b) processes already re-parented to init before `close()` are out of reach, and when an agent quits by itself (W17.2) its helpers are not hunted either. This could be wrong if the author expects idle chats to be reaped, or expects leftover helpers of a chat that ended by itself to be killed. State both as a Hypothesis on W17.1 with its page, what would show it wrong (a leaked process or pty found after a chat the author left idle or that quit on its own), and the evidence to date.
Hypothesis: A chat is closed only on an explicit end (New chat, the screen exiting), never by idle time; and closing reaches only what is still below the agent, so helpers of a chat that quit by itself, or re-parented to init earlier, are left alone. Wrong if you expect idle chats to be reaped or the helpers of a chat that quit on its own to be killed, or a leaked process or pty is found after such a chat. .dfs/artefacts/1c94e0fd-208b-49fd-a17d-4b36e97c4423.html
Evidence:
- for: a `Relay` running `sleep 303` was still live after 4s, and `scripts/ptyrelay.py` has no timer that ends a chat: nothing reaps an idle one.
- for: an agent that exited on its own (rc 0) left its `setsid` helper running (state S) 2s later: nothing hunts it.

Parent: W17.3

'll insert the nodes before the `## Log` section.I logged an `issues` verdict and added two open nodes to `.dfs/items/W17.md`. I changed no code. The working tree outside `.dfs/` is as I found it.

**What holds up.** I ran `test_ptyrelay` and `test_chat`: 31 of 32 pass. I also ran my own probe. It started two chats whose agents ignore SIGHUP (one with a `setsid` helper) and called `close_all()` before the process exited. `close_all()` took 2.04s, and no `sleep` processes were left running afterwards. So W17.1, W17.2, W17.4 and the Ctrl-C path in W17.3 work as described.

**W17.7 · Fix: a TERM or HUP skips all closing.**
- Nothing in `tui.py`, `web.py` or `chat.py` handles SIGTERM or SIGHUP (no `signal.signal` call). Python's default for both is to end the process with no `finally`.
- So `kill`, a service stop, or a dropped ssh session leaves every chat and in-flight turn running, because the closing code only runs on a normal return or Ctrl-C.
- W17.3 made the turn case worse. Turns now start with `start_new_session=True`, so a terminal's hangup no longer reaches them either.
- The node asks for handlers that raise `SystemExit` so the existing cleanup runs, plus a subprocess test with a HUP-ignoring agent. SIGKILL can't be handled and the node says to note that.

**W17.8 · Minor findings.** Six items, all small:
- `Handle.stop` closes chats before it shuts the server down, so a send in that gap starts a turn that survives.
- The `dropped` path in `Chats.turn` has no test.
- `_pump` only reaps a gone agent once the pty has been idle for 0.5s.
- A helper forked after the agent has died is not found by the reaper.
- The W17.3 text about "the walker's chat close" is stale.
- `test_it_will_not_send_while_the_screens_chat_is_open_on_the_session` fails here. I couldn't tell whether the change caused it, because the base checkout fails many tests when extracted to a scratch directory.
